subject: Dedicated reservation — tailored sprint + min-GPU runway for SummitEdge
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@summitedge.com>, Procurement <procurement@summitedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation — tailored sprint + min-GPU runway for SummitEdge

Sara / SummitEdge procurement team —

Great speaking with Sara and the product team yesterday. Per our call, attached is a concise set of dedicated reservation options built to match the SummitEdge pilot and anticipated production ramp. High-level goals we surfaced: keep latency under 120ms p95 for the core inference route, cap monthly token spend to maintain predictable unit economics during ramp, and provide a low-friction path to expand capacity if the pilot receives a go-ahead.

Two packaged offers in the spreadsheet:
- Sprint Starter (12-week pilot): 8 GPUs reserved (mix M60x / Q4 quant profile), boxed burst pool for 2x throughput during testdays, included 1 warm-start window per week. Pricing: $X/month (see sheet). Minimum commitment: 3 months.
- Production Runway: A tiered ladder starting at 24 GPUs minimum, staged activation over 6 months (24 -> 48 -> 96) with defined activation triggers tied to throughput and latency thresholds. Includes prewarming credits and a guaranteed GPU buffer for launch week. Pricing uses step discounts at each break.

Key design choices and rationale:
- Min GPU floor (for Production Runway) set at 24 after modeling: ensures KV cache hit cadence and batching efficiency to hit per-token targets; anything lower degrades latency and raises unit costs.
- Ramp cadence: 8 week observation windows between activations to allow performance telemetry & quantization checks.
- Fallbacks: automated routing to open-model variants if dedicated lane saturates; optional burst from hosted pool to preserve SLA during spikes.

Immediate asks from SummitEdge team: please confirm (a) whether pilot launch is still targeted for early July and (b) whether procurement prefers a single PO for the 6-month runway or separate POs per activation tranche. We can convert the chosen option into a formal SOW and a DocuSign proposal.

Attachments: reserve_options_v2.xlsx (options + pricing), draft-mop-appendix.pdf (MOP and activation triggers).

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@summitedge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-21T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — tailored sprint + min-GPU runway for SummitEdge

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear summary and the options. A couple quick reactions from product + procurement:

1) Pilot timing — July 10 still looks realistic for the internal pilot kickoff, but we need the onboarding runbook and prewarm schedule at least 2 weeks prior.
2) Procurement preference — prefer a single PO for the pilot (Sprint Starter) and then separate POs for subsequent tranches. That keeps our approval flow simpler.
3) Min floor — product agrees that 24 GPUs for initial production seems reasonable; engineering asked if we can front-load an additional 8 GPUs for the first 2 weeks of production to smooth launch-day churn.

Can you confirm whether a short-term 8-GPU burst (hosted burst) can be guaranteed for launch week and included in the proposal as a priced add-on? Also request a 1-page onboarding timeline we can pass to infra.

— Sara
Head of Product Operations | SummitEdge
sara.patel@summitedge.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@summitedge.com>, Procurement <procurement@summitedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-22T08:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — tailored sprint + min-GPU runway for SummitEdge

Sara — thanks. Quick answers inline and a proposed next step.

- Burst for launch week: yes, we can guarantee an 8-GPU hosted burst for a defined 7-day window; pricing is listed as an add-on in reserve_options_v2.xlsx as "Launch Burst (8 GPU, 7d)". That add-on leverages our hosted pool with a reserved allocation during the window and an SLA-backed credit if we fail to deliver capacity.

- Onboarding timeline: drafting a condensed 1-page timeline (onboard-runbook.pdf) and will attach a version for infra by EOD tomorrow. The timeline includes: prewarm window, key telemetry hooks (tracing + token-level cost dashboards), and a cutover checklist.

- Procurement flow: we will structure the DocuSign package to allow a single PO for Sprint Starter and optional tranches for Production Runway. If Procurement still prefers separate POs for later tranches, we'll mark the SOW to reflect staged billing.

Next step: Karthik and Marissa, can you confirm GPU flavor mix for the Sprint Starter (we proposed 6x M60x + 2x Q4 quant nodes) and whether that mix requires any special provisioning lead time? Grace, can you draft the onboarding-runbook.pdf and share the link when ready.

Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@summitedge.com>
Date: 2028-05-23T15:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation — tailored sprint + min-GPU runway for SummitEdge

Thanks Jordan / Sara —

Short answers from infra side:
- GPU mix: confirmed. Sprint Starter: 6x M60x + 2x Q4 quant nodes is fine. No special firmware or whitelist required. We should reserve nodes with the Q4 quant profile enabled to avoid late re-quant windows.
- Provisioning lead time: 10 business days to reserve the dedicated lane and prewarm caches; if SummitEdge signs within 48 hours of the PO we can prioritize and compress to 6 business days but that consumes our prewarm window credits.
- Launch burst: hosted burst add-on is implementable; we'll need the exact 7-day window by EOD June 25 to guarantee capacity.

Operational notes for the SOW: include activation triggers (throughput > X req/s sustained for 72h) and an owner sign-off 48h prior to each tranche activation. Also recommend an initial telemetry holdback of 20% traffic to validate quantized model outputs during the first 72h.

I'll update the technical appendix and push to the shared link (redwood.sharepoint.com/sales/SEQ-4872) by tomorrow morning.

— Karthik Iyer
Head of Deployment Architecture | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
